title: Looking good vs. being right in AI demos

text: Evaluation. How do you actually know an AI's answer is correct, not just convincing? You'll learn why a good demo isn't evidence and what real evidence looks like. If you ever have to trust or approve an AI's output, this is for you. When you judge an answer by reading it,

title: Ground truth and the need for independent grading

title: What makes an honest, representative test set
text: Ground truth, before the model runs so it can't be contaminated. Then let something independent grade. The thing being tested can't be its own judge. If a model checks its own work, it grades against its own assumptions and passes. An independent key catches what it can't see in itself. An evaluation is only as

title: Why a demo is a show but an evaluation is evidence
text: Good as its answer key. If it's easy or you keep tuning against the same test, you get a great-looking score that means nothing. The test set must be honest, held out, representative, and hard. A number you optimize directly against is not evidence. It's a mirror. Before you trust an AI system, look past the demo and ask for the evaluation. Is there an answer key written before the output? Is the grader independent? Could the test have been gamed? Would the result survive on unseen data? A demo is a show. An evaluation is evidence. Ask for the evidence. How do you know an AI is right?
